title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding & Best Practices
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary

This document describes the onboarding checklist and best practices for the Applied-ML evaluation harness at Redwood Inference. It consolidates guidance for: setting up the eval harness, constructing prompt sets and benchmarks, onboarding models, applying quality guardrails, creating quantization profiles, and running a regression triage playbook. The goal is to give new contributors and cross-functional partners a single, actionable reference so model changes are safe, measurable, and repeatable.

Scope

- Audience: ML engineers, applied ML, model ops, SREs, and product owners who operate or rely on model evaluation artifacts.
- Systems covered: eval-harness service, prompt-set catalog, benchmark runner (bench-runner), quality-guardrails service, quantization-profile store.
- Exclusions: ad-hoc human annotation project management (stored in Drive), production rollout runbooks (see rollout pages).

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: Applied ML Infrastructure (engineering).
- On-call and escalation: applied-ml-oncall@redwood.example.com (see oncall rota).
- Tooling owners: bench-runner (team: runtime-eval), prompt-catalog (team: applied-ml).

Onboarding checklist (new model)

1. Read model onboarding template and complete the onboarding request in Pager (use template: model-onboard-request).
2. Create a model entry in the eval catalog with metadata: model_name, model_variant, architecture, trained_vocab, tokenization, expected sequence length distribution, and suggested quantization options.
3. Add baseline prompt sets: correctness, safety, and domain-specific bench sets. Use the prompt naming convention: <team>-<intent>-<granularity>-v01 (example: search-answering-short-v01).
4. Run initial automated benchmarks (latency, throughput, quality) in the staging harness using bench-runner. Record results using the bench-runner artifact uploader.
5. Generate quantization-profile candidates and store them in the quantization-profile repo (see Quantization Profile Checklist below).
6. Create a PR that includes: prompt-set definitions, eval configs, expected metric thresholds, and a summary of initial benchmark results. Assign reviewers from applied-ml and runtime teams.
7. After review and sign-off, mark the model as "onboarded" in the eval catalog and schedule a canary rollout test.

Eval harness architecture (high-level)

- Orchestrator: bench-runner (Kubernetes job-based runner that executes eval shards in parallel).
- Storage: prompt sets and reference outputs are stored in the prompt-catalog (Git-backed) and versioned by tag.
- Metrics: bench-metrics collector -> metrics-store (time-series) and bench-artifacts S3.
- Guardrails: quality-guardrails service listens to eval results and raises alerts when regressions are detected.
- Automation: CI job templates in .github/workflows/bench-runner.yml are used for PR-triggered runs.

Prompt sets and benchmark design

Principles
- Representative: prompt sets must reflect production distribution for the route or product the model will serve.
- Small, deterministic evaluation units: each prompt should be deterministic where possible and include explicit instruction about randomness (temperature, seeds).
- Versioned: every change to a prompt set requires a new version tag and a PR with rationale and metric impact estimate.
- Labeling: prompt sets must include metadata fields: domain, difficulty, expected-answer-type, prevalence-in-prod, and owner.

Prompt set structure (file format)
- JSONL with fields: id, prompt, metadata, expected_outputs (list), tags.
- Example entry: {"id": "pn-0001", "prompt": "Summarize the following text in two sentences:\n...", "metadata": {"domain": "support","difficulty": "medium"}, "expected_outputs": ["Two-sentence summary"]} (prompt-catalog enforces schema).

Benchmark metrics (recommended)
- Quality: BLEU, ROUGE, exact-match, semantic-similarity (embedding-based cosine), human-eval pass-rate (for safety-critical categories).
- Performance: p50/p90 latency (ms), tokens/sec, tail-latency (99th).
- Cost: estimated tokens-per-request, average GPU-seconds per 1k requests.
- Regression thresholds: maintain a per-metric alerting threshold (see Quality Guardrails).

Quality guardrails and acceptance criteria

- Minimum acceptance checks for onboarding:
  - Overall quality metrics >= baseline_quality - 2% (absolute) or within acceptable delta defined by product owner.
  - Safety checks: zero-tolerance categories must have 0% unsafe outputs on the safety prompt set.
  - Latency: p90 latency <= product SLO for the target deployment mode (hosted/dedicated).

- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - Quality regression: a drop of >3% absolute in pass-rate triggers a P1 investigation.
  - Latency regression: p90 increase >40% relative to baseline triggers an operational alert.
  - Cost regression: >20% increase in tokens-per-request or GPU-seconds triggers cost review.

Quantization profile checklist

When proposing quantization profiles for a new model variant, include:
- Target hardware: GPU architecture and CUDA/cuBLAS/other library versions.
- Profile name and tag (e.g., q4_0-int8-hetero-v01).
- Expected quality delta vs FP16 baseline (measured across prompt-sets).
- Recommended operator fallbacks or kernel overrides.
- Memory and throughput impact estimates.

Sample quantization profile (YAML fragment):

---
profile_name: q4_0-int8-hetero-v01
target_hardware: NVIDIA-A100-40GB
quant_scheme: q4_0
per_layer_overrides:
  - layer_range: 0-12
    fallback: fp16
metrics_expectation:
  semsim_delta_pct: "<=1.5"
  rouge_delta_points: "<=0.8"
---

Bench-runner CI and reproducibility

- All PRs that modify prompt-sets or eval configs must include a bench-runner CI job that executes a smoke eval (subset) and uploads metrics.
- For full-bench runs, include explicit seed values and artifact links in PR description.
- Reproducibility: bench artifacts must contain: git commit of model code, model binary hash, tokenizer version, random seed, and bench-runner invocation command.

Regression triage playbook (high-level)

1. Detection: alert from quality-guardrails or bench-runner indicates a regression. Include links to failing prompt-set examples and related artifacts.
2. Triage ownership: assign to applied-ml oncall. Determine whether regression is: model change, quantization, data drift, prompt change, or infra change.
3. Quick rollback: if regression is production-impacting and root cause is uncertain, execute rollback plan (use tagged previous model variant).
4. Narrowing down: run controlled A/B bench runs comparing the last two known-good commits across: full prompt set, safety prompts, and a targeted triage subset (10-50 prompts).
5. Fix or mitigate: apply a fix (model patch, quantization profile change, prompt rewrite) and run full bench-runner.
6. Postmortem: for any P1 regression, publish a postmortem with timeline, root cause, impact, and action items within 72 hours.

Runbook: immediate steps for an alerted regression

- Step 0: Acknowledge the alert and create an incident ticket with tags: regression, model-name, metric, severity.
- Step 1: Collect bench artifacts: bench artifact URL, commit hashes, quantization profile used, and sample failing outputs.
- Step 2: Re-run bench-runner with last-known-good model vs current model on the triage subset.
- Step 3: If evidence shows quantization is root cause, switch to the last-known-good quantization profile and validate.
- Step 4: If it's a model code change, coordinate immediate rollback with runtime and infra teams.
- Step 5: Notify product stakeholders and downstream consumers using the customer-impact channel.

SLOs and key metrics for the eval process

- CI coverage: 100% of prompt-set PRs must run smoke evals in CI.
- Regression detection latency: median time from commit to regression alert <= 6 hours.
- Reproducibility: bench artifacts are archived for 180 days.
- Onboarding time: median time from initial onboarding PR to accepted onboarding <= 14 days for standard models.

Templates and CLI examples

- Run a bench-runner smoke eval (example):
  ./bench-runner --model-tag rwd-model-v1 --prompt-set support-smoke-v01 --seeds 42 --out artifacts/rwd-model-v1-smoke.json

- Upload bench artifact:
  bench-uploader upload --artifact artifacts/rwd-model-v1-smoke.json --project applied-ml --tags "smoke,onboard"

- Create a quantization profile PR: include YAML profile, measured deltas, and commands to reproduce quantization steps.

Related pages and references

- Model onboarding template: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/model-onboard-template
- Quantization profiles best practices: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
- Bench-runner repo README and CI workflows: github.com/redwood/bench-runner (internal)

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations

- Flaky prompts: move flaky prompts into an "unstable" tag and exclude from blocking pass-rate metrics.
- Non-deterministic tokenization differences: pin tokenizer version and tokenization tests in CI.
- Infrastructure contention causing latency spikes: re-run bench with dedicated node pool and isolate infra variables.

Document maintenance

- Owner is responsible for an annual review of this page. Changes to onboarding or acceptance criteria must be recorded in the page history and communicated on the Applied-ML weekly sync.

Contact

For questions or exceptions, contact the page owner: Asha Patel (asha.patel@redwood.example.com) or the applied-ml team channel on Slack: #applied-ml.
